patch.value: Push refuses a non-fast-forward and lands every ref under compare-and-swap

A push writes to a repository other agents are also writing to, so both hazards are real: overwriting history the remote has and the pusher has not seen, and racing another pusher between the check and the write. The first is refused by requiring the remote's current tip to be an ancestor of the pushed commit, including the case where the remote's tip is absent from the pusher's own store, which is not a fast-forward that can be verified at all and must say so rather than assume. The second is closed by making every ref update a compare-and-swap against the value the pusher observed.

A push whose remote tip is not an ancestor of the pushed commit is refused with a message naming the ref; force overrides the refusal; a push whose remote tip is not present locally is refused as unverifiable and tells the agent to fetch first; a concurrent update between observation and write fails the push rather than clobbering; the pushed refs are recorded in the receiving repository's operation log so a force push stays reversible; a push transfers only objects the remote lacks
